text:
Ottawa comes to Pittsburgh on a high after beating Colorado 4-3 in overtime on Thursday, a game the Senators trailed in the third period and Shane Pinto won in the extra frame. They're 3-1-1 in their last five and are missing Nick Cousins, Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele, plus William Eklund, whose minutes beside Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund have gone to Tim Stützle. Pittsburgh is 2-3-0 over its last five and won at San Jose in a shootout, a night Mason Marchment reached 100 career goals. The Penguins are without Bryan Rust, and Evgeni Malkin has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell.

Our numbers see almost nothing between them: our model has Ottawa at 3.15 expected goals (the quality of chances, not just their count) and Pittsburgh at 3.13, with both teams at 52% of the five-on-five expected goals. Pittsburgh gives up more chances (3.41 per 60 against 2.98 for Ottawa), while Ottawa takes 4.7 penalties a game. Neither projected goalie has been sharp. Samuel Ersson is at -1.13 goals saved above expected this season (-17.75 last year), and Sergei Murashov is at -0.54 (-3.52 in five games last year).

Watch Stützle, drafted third overall in 2020 out of Adler Mannheim, at 35% to score. Crosby is at 34% and Malkin at 28%. Philip Tomasino plays his first game in Pittsburgh since leaving the Penguins, and is one point from 100 career points. Our under-the-radar pick is Zetterlund, a third-liner with 3.2 expected goals in his last 10 games, at 18% to score.
